subject: Re: Renewal evidence & retention — escrow and scalable retention options
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@novuscorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: audit@novuscorp.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: SOC 2 re-attestation evidence + retention options

Hi Rachel,

Our renewal for the NovusCorp contract is coming up in June and Procurement asked me to confirm the security attestation path. We need Redwood's SOC 2 recertification package and a short proposal on log retention and escrow options for audit. Specifically: 

- A list of artifacts you can provide for SOC 2 re-attestation (control mappings, sample audit logs, evidence pull process).
- Options and pricing for retention beyond the default (90 days) — we are evaluating 1 year retention for critical audit logs.
- Any recommended process for handing an evidence snapshot to an auditor (SFTP/secure upload, escrow, or on-demand access).
- Whether a temporary capacity bump is required to produce a full snapshot and a rough lead time.

Can you share an initial checklist and an estimated timeline? Procurement will want a simple amendment we can sign; if you can include a ballpark for the retention uplift + any one-off transfer costs that would help accelerate the internal review.

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Park
Head of Compliance, NovusCorp
lyn: +1 415 555 0192

Putting the short version up front: we can support SOC 2 re-attestation evidence pulls, offer a 365-day retention tier, and provide an evidence snapshot workflow (secure, auditable transfer). There may be a temporary cost for the snapshot transfer depending on volume; I9ll share options below and loop in Security and CS for details.

Attached: novus_evidence_checklist_v1.pdf (initial mapping).

- Kimberly to confirm artifacts and transfer options.
- Ben to propose a mutual action plan (dry run + amendment timeline).

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Lydia Park <lydia.park@novuscorp.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-20T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: SOC 2 re-attestation evidence + retention options

Hi all — quick operational rundown and options. Thanks Rachel and Lydia.

What we can provide for SOC 2 re-attestation:
- Control mapping document (we map Redwood controls to common SOC 2 criteria).
- Sample policy artifacts (incident response, change control summaries).
- Redacted sample logs and a log sampling plan.
- Evidence pull procedure with chain-of-custody (we produce an evidence manifest and MD5 checksums).

Retention and transfer options (summary):
1) Standard: 90-day rolling retention, included in current plan — no additional contract change.
2) Extended archival: 365-day retention for audit logs — add-on priced monthly (see quote attached).
   - Storage delta estimate for Novus (based on current ingestion): ~1.2 TB/month => incremental $X/month (see retention_quote_v2.xlsx).
3) Escrow / one-time snapshot: we can produce a point-in-time export in two flavors:
   - Secure transfer (SFTP to client auditor account) — minimal ops overhead; one-time transfer fee based on GB.
   - Evidence escrow: we package artifacts into an encrypted archive and deposit with our third-party escrow partner; includes notarized manifest.

Capacity/throughput notes: producing a full snapshot (log export + evidence bundle) for your volume will require a short burst of dedicated capacity for ~6-12 hours. We can schedule it during a low-traffic window; typical lead time 3-5 business days to schedule and validate. If you want a repeated dry run prior to the auditor, plan +7 business days.

What I need from Novus:
- Confirmation of desired retention window (90d vs 365d).
- Preferred transfer method for the audit (SFTP vs escrow).
- Target audit date and auditor contact for credentials.

Attachments: retention_quote_v2.xlsx, log_archive_manifest.csv (sample manifest).

I9ll produce a short mutual action plan doc once Lydia confirms the choices.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@novuscorp.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: SOC 2 re-attestation evidence + retention options

Lydia / Rachel — I can run the mutual action plan and calendar. Proposed timeline (draft):

- Week 0 (this week): Novus confirms retention choice + transfer method. I9ll create a PoC dry-run SOW (1 page).
- Week 1: Security executes a dry run export into a staging SFTP (we validate manifest).
- Week 2: Auditor validation (if they want direct access) or escrow handoff.
- Week 3: Contract amendment drafted and routed to Procurement; DocuSign ready for signature.

Ballpark costs: retention uplift (365d) + one-time snapshot transfer = estimated $8k-$12k depending on transfer size and escrow option. I9ll get a precise number after Kimberly sends the storage delta.

Scheduling: I have a 30-min slot Thursday 2:00–2:30pm PT if Procurement wants a live walkthrough. Otherwise I9ll post the short plan to the HubSpot deal and attach the amendment draft for Procurement review.

Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@novuscorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@novuscorp.com, audit@novuscorp.com
Date: 2027-04-21T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: SOC 2 re-attestation evidence + retention options

Thanks, everyone — this is helpful. We9ll proceed with the 365-day retention and prefer the escrowed evidence package for the final audit (auditor will not have direct SFTP). Procurement asked that you include the one-time snapshot transfer and the monthly delta in a single amendment line item for ease of approval.

Please:
- Kimberly: confirm the final storage delta and the one-time transfer fee so we can lock the numbers.
- Ben: please start the amendment draft and include the dry-run SOW.
- Rachel: once we have the numbers we will circulate to Procurement and expect a quick DocuSign.

Can we aim to have a ready-to-sign amendment within 10 business days? If you need anything from our side (auditor contact, credentials for escrow acceptance), I9ll push it through today.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Lydia
Lydia Park
Head of Compliance, NovusCorp
